source_snapshot.procedure: Test connections between Strata CPU and RTC on SMM.
source_snapshot.criteria: CPU/OS can successfully communicate with RTC and read time.
source_snapshot.script: No bundle; 10 attended/10 machine minutes; unique row/variant.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; proposes a BMC-side I2C scan plus operator photos, which does not prove the specified CPU/OS RTC path.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION/MEDIUM; held Pending for CPU/OS-to-SMM path mapping, RTC device/driver identity, read semantics, trusted reference/tolerance, physical proof and recovery.

old_problem: BMC-side address visibility cannot prove CPU/OS communication with the SMM RTC. The row omits the OS RTC device mapping, time scale/reference/tolerance and handling of validity, update/latch and rollover, while clock or register writes would alter the condition under test.
disposition_reason: Linux exposes RTC devices and read-only sysfs attributes, and util-linux hwclock can explicitly select and read a named RTC device. These authoritative standard interfaces support a safe parameterized case: bind the project-specific SMM RTC to one OS device/driver, collect read-only identity/status and repeated samples, and compare progression against a preapproved reference/tolerance. No raw bus probing or clock setting is needed.
decision_basis: XLSX row 2163, same-row DeepSeek columns, GPT V2, historical record, unique identity and ED-01 through ED-30 were reviewed; actual next formal row Functionality 2164 / Wistron-GB NV PVP HW-00051-V002 / f7f71f689164af82 was directly read from XLSX and manifest.
Linux RTC documentation establishes `/sys/class/rtc/rtcN` read-only attributes and support for multiple RTC devices, so the exact SMM-bound device must be selected rather than assuming rtc0.
util-linux hwclock `--show` reads the Hardware Clock and `--rtc=filename` selects the device; direct ISA access is explicitly avoided.
Bind the CPU/OS-to-SMM architecture, device/driver and trusted reference/tolerance as Project Configuration; operator photos preserve the physical-path requirement.
Capture multiple timestamped samples, device identity/driver/status and kernel RTC evidence; account for second-boundary rollover and approved UTC/local interpretation.
Prohibit `--set`, `--systohc`, `--hctosys`, direct ISA, RTC/register writes, time changes, raw unknown I2C access, reset and automatic retry.
No RTC read, bus query, physical manipulation, clock change, write, reset, retry or DUT action was performed.

test_case.test_name: CPU/OS-bound SMM RTC identity and read-only time-progression validation
test_case.purpose: Prove the Strata CPU/OS is bound to the intended RTC on the SMM and can read a valid, progressing time through the approved OS interface, with physical-path evidence and no clock modification.
required_package: Approved CPU/OS-to-SMM RTC architecture and operator physical inspection/photos
Exact OS RTC device and driver binding plus hardware endpoint identity
util-linux hwclock or equivalent approved read-only RTC interface
RTC validity/status, UTC/local interpretation, trusted reference and tolerance policy
Kernel/RTC log collection, abort and non-writing recovery procedure
test_case.test_command: BLOCKED until Project Configuration is signed. Operator verifies and photographs the CPU-to-SMM RTC path. Record the mapped `/sys/class/rtc/rtcN` identity/driver/status and use `hwclock --show --rtc <approved-device>` or the approved equivalent for multiple timestamped read-only samples; compare validity, monotonic progression and reference tolerance without setting either clock.
test_case.expected_result: The approved OS RTC device is demonstrably the SMM endpoint, its driver/status is valid, repeated reads advance coherently and remain within the signed reference tolerance, and no kernel/RTC/I2C/management fault or time change occurs.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires target-bound physical/device evidence, valid advancing samples and signed tolerance compliance. FAIL on wrong device/path, invalid or stopped/backward/implausible time, tolerance breach or platform fault. Missing mapping/tolerance is runtime BLOCKED; BMC-only visibility is insufficient.
safety_gate: Gate CLOSED until device mapping, read-only command, time interpretation/tolerance and recovery are signed.
No clock set/synchronization action, direct ISA access, raw unknown bus read/write or RTC control/register write.
Operator-only physical inspection; do not disturb the SMM connection.
Stop on wrong-device mapping, invalid/oscillator-stop status, implausible jump, bus error or management instability; no automatic retry.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, approval and CPU/SMM/RTC path photos
OS RTC device/driver/hardware binding and complete read-only sysfs/status inventory
Exact read-only command, device path and UTC/local/reference policy
Multiple timestamped RTC samples with rollover-aware progression and tolerance calculation
Pre/post kernel/RTC/I2C/BMC evidence and proof clocks were not changed
test_case.recovery: On invalid time, wrong mapping or bus/platform fault, stop and preserve all samples/logs. Do not set either clock, write RTC registers, reset the bus or retry automatically; follow the approved non-writing platform recovery and escalate if the device/path cannot be verified.

source_conflict.reason: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require CPU/OS access to the SMM RTC; the BMC-only proposal is rejected as non-equivalent.

blocked.reason: Standard Linux read-only RTC semantics provide a safe method; device mapping, physical proof and tolerance are runtime project bindings rather than unresolved core commands.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: CPU/OS-to-SMM RTC mapping, exact OS device/driver, read-only command, status semantics, UTC/local interpretation, trusted reference/tolerance, photos, abort and recovery.
pending.execution_status: REVIEW RESOLVED; PARAMETERIZED READ-ONLY RTC GATE CLOSED; NO READ, BUS QUERY, PHYSICAL MANIPULATION, CLOCK CHANGE, WRITE, RESET, RETRY OR DUT ACTION EXECUTED
pending.owner: Platform/RTC firmware and OS owner, hardware service owner and time-policy authority
pending.unlock_condition: Bind the signed SMM RTC device mapping, read-only method and time oracle and authorize inspection/read; no new review decision is required absent architecture change.

external_authorities.application: Multiple RTC devices and read-only `/sys/class/rtc/rtcN` attributes support device-bound, non-writing evidence.
`--show` reads the Hardware Clock and `--rtc` selects the device; direct hardware access is avoided.
Requires target-bound evidence, manual physical proof, authoritative tolerance, safe recovery and no guessed or state-changing command.

project_authority: Platform/RTC owner binds the SMM endpoint and status semantics; OS owner approves the device/command; time authority approves reference/tolerance; service owner provides physical proof; engineer owns verdict.
